newsitem.title: USA: DC control board names interim agency chiefs.
newsitem.headline: DC control board names interim agency chiefs.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board Tuesday took its first steps under Congress' new rehabilitation plan for the city by naming interim heads of nine embattled city departments.

At a public meeting interrupted repeatedly by protestors, the board named temporary heads for administrative services, consumer and regulatory affairs, corrections, employment services, housing and community development, human services, public works and public health.

"We will not run from responsibility," control board member Joyce Ladner said at the opening of the meeting, which was delayed nearly an hour by demonstrators yelling "treason" and the "the time has come for the Potomac Tea Party."

President Clinton on Tuesday signed the National Capital Revitalization Act passed by Congress last week. The measure seeks major management reforms and turns over extensive control of city operations to the five-member control board.
"While the authority did not seek this responsibility, we will not shrink from it," D.C. control board chairman Andrew Brimmer told the crowd meeting at a downtown church.
The panel must move "decisively and swiftly," Brimmer said, noting that the law requires it to develop management reform plans within 90 days for the nine District departments.
The acting directors, whose names were recommended by D.C. Mayor Marion Barry, will run the departments until permanent heads are cleared by the control board, Brimmer said.

He said acting directors will report directly to the control board, in a move that protestors said exceeds the board's authority. "You have taken the position that you have control of daily operations," said one citizen. "The (new) law does not speak to that issue."
Some protestors urged control board members to step down rather than allow Congress to "suspend" Democracy in the District through the new law.
"You marched for freedom and went to jail," one demonstrator told Ladner, a former civil rights worker. "How could you serve on this board. You must step down.
"While you have Congress and the President on your side, you do not have the U.S. Constitution on your side."
But Ladner said those who think the control board is "lusting" for power are wrong.
"We didn't ask for this legislation. I don't want it," he said. "(But) I ask each of you to work with us to achieve these goals so that D.C. can once again live up to its potential."

The control board appointed the following officials as temporary department heads: Richard Fite, administrative services; David Watts, consumer and regulatory affairs and housing and community development; Maragaret Moore, corrections; Alexis Roberson, employment services, Donald Edwards, fire and emergency services; Jearline Williams, human services; Cellerino Bernardino, public works; and Robert Noonan, public health.
